item.description: Guten Morgen! The New England Patriots are overseas in Munich, Germany to take on the Detroit Lions in their Week 10 matchup. NFC North opponents haven’t been kind to the Patriots this season, as they are 0-2 against the division. That includes last week’s 45-27 drubbing to the Green Bay Packers, which sets the stage for an important bounce-back game in Germany ahead of the team’s bye week. Let’s find out which Patriots team will show up Sunday. Welcome to our Patriots-Lions live tracker and community discussion. New England’s offense moved the ball well to quickly work into the red zone behind a 26-yard flea flicker to Mack Hollins. Two pre-snap penalties and a third-sack in the red zone by Aidan Hutchinson working against Will Campbell, however, limited the group to an opening drive field goal. [Patriots 3 : 0 Lions] After Detroit picked up an opening first-down, Jared Goff hit Amon-Ra St. Brown short of the sticks on third-down before the receiver made Christian Gonzalez miss to take it 56 yards to the house. With DeVito still in the game, the Patriots offense went backwards on their first two offensive plays which led to another three-and-out. item.title: Bainbridge, Central Kitsap volleyball teams collect trophies
item.description: For the second consecutive season, Bainbridge's volleyball team left the Class 2A state tournament at the Yakima Valley SunDome with a trophy. Placing 7th at state in 2025, the Spartans earned 6th place on Saturday, Nov. 14 after finishing 2-2 during the two-day tournament. Bainbridge wrapped up its season with 21-2 record. Winning the Olympic League title and West Central District championship, Bainbridge drew the No. 5 seed at state and opened Friday with a 3-1 win over No. 12 Mark Morris. The Spartans then lost 3-0 in the quarterfinals against No. 4 Ridgefield, which ended up winning the 2A title over No. 2 Ellensburg. On Saturday, Bainbridge won 3-1 against No. 9 Orting in an elimination match before the Spartans fell 3-0 against No. 3 Pullman in the 5th/6th-place game. North Kitsap (13-8) qualified for state as well. The Vikings went 0-2, dropping 3-1 matches against Pullman and No. 11 Selah. Central Kitsap tops Timberline for district title Central Kitsap will head to next week's 3A state tournament in Yakima with plenty of momentum. The Cougars captured the West Central District championship Saturday at Mount Tahoma High School by knocking off Timberline 3-1. It was the Blazers' first defeat of the season. In the semifinals, Central Kitsap beat defending 3A champion North Thurston 3-1. Central Kitsap (18-3) will learn its state seed on Sunday when the 3A brackets are released. The 3A tournament runs Nov. 20-21. The Cougars placed 6th last season. This article originally appeared on Kitsap Sun: Bainbridge, Central Kitsap volleyball teams collect trophies

There’s always a lot of pressure on his own serve. It was a tough first out for him. I think he acquitted himself pretty well, really. I think he’s probably more excited about other matches that he’s got to come. “For me, it was just interesting to watch the dad. I sat a few seats down from him. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons host the Kansas City Chiefs , looking to bounce back with a win against one of the decade’s most successful teams. With the Chiefs in the thick of contention at the top of the AFC, they’re a litmus test for whether the Falcons can knock off another top team and pull off a home upset like they did three weeks ago against San Francisco . Five Falcons will be among the most tested in this matchup. Michael Penix Jr. The formidable Chiefs defense will be another big test for Michael Penix, thanks to defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. Spags’ strategy will likely lean on blitzing Penix to exploit his struggles under pressure and using disguised coverages to confuse the young quarterback. For Penix’s evaluation, it’s important to see how he handles one of the NFL’s most challenging defensive schemes and stays poised amid the controlled chaos. Bijan Robinson Bijan Robinson, along with the Falcons’ run game, will be tasked with taking pressure off Penix, but will be tested against one of the NFL’s best run defenses. Whatever category you want to measure, whether it’s yards, yards per carry, EPA, or yards before and after contact, the Chiefs rank among the top 10 teams across the board . Facing four other Top 11-ranked run defenses so far this year, Robinson has averaged 76.5 yards per game and 4.6 yards per carry. That looks impressive at face value, but his success rate in those games was 36 percent, which ranks among the bottom 5 in the NFL, according to NextGenStats . As the NFL’s leading rusher, Robinson has racked up most of his production against lesser defenses, averaging 115 yards per game, 5.6 yards per carry, with a second-ranked 52 percent success rate in his five other outings. Essentially, the numbers show that the quality of competition dictates the Falcons’ success when establishing the run. Given the Chiefs’ stout defense, it’s another huge trial to see whether this trend continues. item.title: Triumph or flop? The Rugby League World Cup that split opinion
item.description: The winning captains: Australia's Isabelle Kelly, her men's counterpart Isaah Yeo and England wheelchair skipper Lewis King [Getty Images] Has the 2026 Rugby League World Cup been a success or not? It depends on who you listen to - and perhaps where in the world you are. The men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments provided plenty of stories - from Kalyn Ponga's return from a broken arm in 23 days, to Jodie Cunningham's mangled ear, to the England wheelchair team's golden ladder, to the men's group format that caused widespread bafflement. But was the World Cup a triumph? The northern and southern hemisphere perspectives provide contrasting answers. For the fourth tournament running, Australia won the men's and women's titles, with New Zealand unable to deliver a twist in either final. Tonga and Samoa brought vibrancy and passion - performing to a level that underlined why they are being elevated to Tier One status. The large Polynesian population in the USA - which will co-host the 2030 men's and women's World Cups - is likely to be key in spreading the rugby league word further around the world. England's Wheelchair World Cup win, in a thunderous final against their old foes France, offset some of the disappointment felt when Brian McDermott's men and Stuart Barrow's women went home early. And unlike when the game was emerging from post-pandemic constraints in 2022, the tournament has also worked financially by posting a profit. "This whole tournament's been incredible," said Australia men's captain Isaah Yeo. "Not just the fans here for New Zealand and Australia, but just everyone. I thought it was all outstanding. "I think it's to date the most competitive and the best World Cup there's been. I think that's only going to continue to grow." That sentiment has been endorsed repeatedly by Australian television broadcaster Channel Seven, which paid a reported A$12m (£6.1m) for exclusive domestic free-to-air coverage of the men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments. Not everyone has been able to feel that positivity, though. The decision to cut the men's tournament from 16 teams to 10 reduced the overall number of matches - and deprived teams such as Jamaica and Greece of a chance to build on the feelgood factor they provided as debutants in 2022. That decision was made after Australia stepped in to stage the tournament, postponed for a year when scheduled hosts France pulled out for financial reasons. For those who did get to the party this time, it has not always been an even contest. The disparity between the haves and have-nots has been significant. While the Jillaroos and Kangaroos players will each receive equal payments of $40,000 (£20,500) for competing, Wales will reportedly spread a total of $15,000 (£7,689) across their women's and wheelchair teams. item.title: Zverev claims first win as world number one at ATP Finals
item.description: Alexander Zverev has won 66 ATP Tour matches this season - the most of any men's player [Getty Images] Alexander Zverev claimed his first victory as world number one as he swept aside Rafael Jodar in the opening match of the ATP Finals. Germany's Zverev produced a serving masterclass to beat the fast-rising Spaniard 6-4 6-4. The French and US Open champion dropped only 10 points on serve, landing an astonishing 84% of first serves and hitting 10 aces. The only time Zverev looked troubled was when he went two break points down as he served for the opening set - before saving them with back-to-back aces. "I still think I have a lot of things to improve. It was not a perfect match but to start the tournament, I am very happy," the 29-year-old said. "Winning always helps, but it's been a good match." Zverev lost his first match as world number one at the Paris Masters in November and said afterwards he was "annoyed" at the reaction to his rise to the top of the rankings. He has taken full advantage of a year in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have struggled with injuries, winning two majors and reaching the Wimbledon final. Zverev underlined his status as the world's best player by walking out on court in Turin in a custom black leather jacket with a number one printed on the back. His performance was just as befitting of his position as he put constant pressure on the Jodar serve and dominated with his own first strike. The 20-year-old Jodar is one of the brightest talents in the men's game, having started the year outside the world's top 150. Now ranked 11th, he fought hard to stay in touch with Zverev, but could find no way through his serve. Zverev broke him early in the first set with a fine backhand down the line and went up a quick break in the second. He had three further chances for a double-break lead but Jodar saved them, before Zverev served out victory. In the doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara began their campaign with a 6-3 5-7 10-4 win over Brazilian pair Rafael Matos and Orlando Luz. Wimbledon champions Patten and Heliovaara are the defending champions in Turin. Pochettino targets Craven Cottage skipper to plug leaky backline According to The Telegraph , Fulham defender Calvin Bassey has emerged as a surprise candidate to bolster Manchester United's porous defence when the transfer window reopens in January. Appointed last week to replace Michael Carrick , Pochettino has wasted little time assessing the personnel at Old Trafford and views a new centre-half as a top priority. The former Rangers and Ajax defender enters the final year of his current contract, though the west London club hold an option to extend his stay by a further 12 months. Versatility and full-back shortages drive Old Trafford interest Bassey’s capacity to operate effectively at left-back is understood to be a major draw for Pochettino as he weighs up his tactical options. item.title: What Paul McGinley noticed about Tyrrell Hatton’s behavior during the final round in Dubai
item.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Tyrrell Hatton won the sixth Rolex Series event of his career on Sunday in Dubai after he clinched the DP World Tour Championship at the Earth Course. Hatton played some truly wonderful golf this week in Dubai, especially during the final round as he posted a score of 66 to win the tournament by five shots. Unfortunately for the 35-year-old, his victory procession over the back nine seemed like nothing more than a subplot as Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra battled it out for the Race to Dubai title. However, Tyrrell Hatton won’t care about that whatsoever. Hatton admitted to being ‘weirdly nervous’ before the final round in Dubai on Sunday, but he obviously harnessed those feelings to good use. Now he can call himself a six-time Rolex Series winner. What Paul McGinley noticed about Tyrrell Hatton’s behavior in Dubai After Hatton’s victory at the Earth Course on Sunday, Sky Sports commentators Paul McGinley and Nick Dougherty highlighted how they noticed a big change in the Englishman’s behavior during the final round. “ I would say personally, watching him across the last two days, he looked a little bit more restrained, “ Dougherty said. “ He looked a little bit more in control of his emotions. It looked like it was a peak Hatton, across those last two days. He really was head shoulders above across the tournament this week. “ Then McGinley chimed in with his opinion on the matter. “ Yeah, I think your point that better behavior from him results in better golf is the correct one. I see that, “ McGinley replied. “ When he got control of the tournament and got ahead, the moaning and groaning seemed to stop, and he seemed to go into overdrive, and he was a little softer on himself. “ You know, he ran off with it, he lapped the field with a five-shot lead. Everybody else got distracted with the Race to Dubai, and he just kept going forward. “ Perhaps Tyrrell Hatton has reached an age now where he has become slightly more easygoing. It was obvious to see that he wasn’t as harsh on himself during the final round in Dubai as he usually is. And if his new-found positive attitude resulted in the golf we saw him produce this week, he may well be a real force in the professional game over the next decade or so.

item.title: When Michael Jordan’s agent revealed Nike’s $3 million fail-safe if Bulls legend flopped
item.description: Photo by Bongarts/Getty Images Nike took all measures in Michael Jordan failed to become a global basketball superstar. When the Chicago Bulls selected Michael Jordan using the third overall pick in the 1984 NBA Draft, no one knew he would become a global sensation. Evidently, when Jordan signed a groundbreaking deal with Nike that included a signature shoe and royalties, it shocked the NBA community to its core. At the time, Nike wasn’t a gigantic corporation, and if trusting MJ had failed, it could have spelt trouble for the company. As a result, Nike tried to play it safe, as revealed by MJ’s agent, David Falk. David Falk once revealed Nike’s escape clause for Michael Jordan During a 2023 appearance on ‘The 20 & 20 Podcast,’ Falk revealed details about his conversation with Nike’s then-marketing head, Rob Strasser. Falk revealed how Nike wanted to insert stat-based clauses in Jordan’s contract with the sneaker company. “That makes no sense. You’re not an NBA team; what do you care what his statistics are? All you should care about is how many shoes he’s selling. “He said, ‘I’ll give you a number. If in the end of the third year, as we head into the fourth year, if we haven’t sold $3 million worth of shoes, we want to be able to stop making the shoe.’ I said no problem,” Falk recalled. He added, “We’ll honor the contract for the full five years, we’ll pay him every dollar he’s owed, but if he doesn’t make Rookie of the Year in his rookie year, or in the first three years, he doesn’t average 20 points a game ever, doesn’t ever make the All-Star team, we want to be able to stop making the shoe.” That $3 million target was Nike’s fail-safe in case Jordan never became a superstar. However, Falk then revealed how the Chicago Bulls guard smashed Nike’s expectations. “They thought selling 3 million will be like hitting a grand slam home run, and Michael sold 126 million in the first year. He sold roughly 40 percent probably of all Nike shoes,” Falk stated. Today, the Jordan Brand is a massive money-making machine for Nike and reportedly generates over $7 billion in annual revenue. item.title: San Antonio is most popular location for an NFL team expansion, survey finds
item.description: Nineteen percent of the 1,000 NFL fans surveyed by Betway Insider said they would like to see a franchise in the Alamo City. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) San Antonio is the city NFL fans most want to see get a team, a new survey found. Nineteen percent of the 1,000 NFL fans surveyed by Betway Insider said they would like to see a franchise in the Alamo City, making it the most popular choice for an expansion team. San Antonio edged out Oklahoma City by just seven votes, despite both cities receiving 19% of the vote. The Lone Star state already has two NFL teams, the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans, but that didn't stop fans from calling for more. Austin took fifth place in the survey, with 14% of respondents saying they'd like to see a team there. READ MORE : 5 final thoughts from Cowboys-49ers: Can Dallas earn respect with upset of San Francisco? There have been periodic discussions among National Football League executives about expanding the league, but no new team has joined since 2002, when the Houston Texans were established. Thirteen percent of respondents said they don't think expansion is currently necessary. International expansion was the least popular among respondents. Just 9% of voters said London, which has hosted more NFL games than any other international city, should have its own team. Dublin and Munich received 4% and 2% of the vote, respectively. But even if the NFL were to expand, San Antonio faces several hurdles. The Alamodome lacks revenue-generating amenities like luxury suites and club seating, meaning San Antonio would likely need a new stadium to accommodate an NFL team. The city would also likely face pushback from Cowboys and Texans executives, whose teams currently share the San Antonio market. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.description: Texas State Bobcats offensive lineman Justin DeLeon (66) celebrates after beating the Fresno State Bulldogs 37-35 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 14, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) SAN MARCOS - Texas State football found a way to win Saturday night, clinching a 37-35 victory over Fresno State in a type of game that the Bobcats used to lose, often in heartbreaking fashion. The Bobcats (6-4, 4-2 Pac-12) made a habit of squandering leads in 2025, and have done so three times in 2026. But the hardships they endured toughened Texas State's resolve, head coach GJ Kinne said, and it showed in the fourth quarter against Fresno State (5-5, 2-4). "Sometimes adversity early on in the season, as bad as it is … I think it helped us tonight and in that fourth quarter," Kinne said. MORE: Bobcats squeeze out win over Bulldogs 'Next play mentality' for Texas State Texas State got off to an explosive start, scoring touchdowns on four straight drives. The offense cooled as rain poured down in the second half. It entered halftime up 28-21 and the lead evaporated when Fresno State running back Bryson Donelson scored in the fourth quarter to put his team up 35-31. The Bulldogs put on a coaching clinic, Kinne said. Fresno State quarterback Jayden Mandal was nails on third down, converting 8 of 13 attempts. The Bulldogs pulled off a fake field goal in the third quarter with kicker Ryan Kobzeff running in a 19-yard touchdown. And when Texas State running back Torrance Burgess Jr. fumbled at the 1-yard line with just under six minutes remaining, the outlook seemed bleak. But Bobcats defensive back Michael Patterson III had other ideas. Patterson said Mandal had been trying to look him off all game. He didn't bite on third-and-11, undercutting the quarterback's throw for an interception with 3 minutes and 39 seconds left. "We hadn't played our best game up to that point," Patterson said. "But it's always a next-play mentality." Texas State Bobcats wide receiver Jordan Martin (14) celebrates after beating the Fresno State Bulldogs 37-35 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 14, 2026. Quarterback Brad Jackson, who threw for 355 yards and three touchdowns, came up big on the final drive. Facing a fourth-and-2 in Fresno State territory, he ripped a quick slant to wide receiver Chris Dawn Jr. for a first down. Dawn set the program record for career receptions in the second quarter, and on that clutch catch, showed why Kinne has believed in him since his days at Mesquite Horn High School. "That's the play we've been missing, right?" Kinne said. "Last time we've been in these situations, we haven't got it done." item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: (R-L) Luis Gurule punches Bilal Hasan in their flyweight fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) DING DING DING — it happened again. Undefeated Bilal Hasan entered UFC 334 as an absolutely monstrous favorite over Luis Gurule . The 25-year-old Hasan was expected to run over his older opponent, who entered the bout with just one victory in five previous trips to the Octagon. There was an obvious outcome that pretty much everybody predicted: Hasan — the tall and lanky prospect with shades of Sean O’Malley in his standup — should pick apart the unheralded Gurule. Public confidence was so high that Hasan swelled up to an 11-1 favorite. As it turns out, styling on UFC fighters (even unsung ones) isn’t so easy. Gurule had already spent nearly an hour inside the Octagon accruing experience against solid opposition, and that valuable time cannot be purchased or undercut. Just like that, it’s FRAUD CHECK time. Another big prospect suffers their first career defeat in record-setting circumstances, and countless parlays are busted in agonizing fashion for degenerates around the globe. It’s an increasingly frequent story, and this particular instance breaks down into a trio of components. First and foremost: the odds are f—king insane nowadays. Prediction markets are pushing odds to outrageous numbers. Everyone has access to nearly unregulated sports betting, and thus “historic” odds are appearing every other month. 10-0 is not that many wins. 25 years old is quite young. A young and green prospect should never be an 11-1 favorite over a more experienced opponent who, at a minimum, has proven himself capable of competing with established UFC talent. We’re not even talking about an Olympic gold medalist in a weak division like Gable Steveson — Hasan just has a nice highlight reel over names nobody reading this has ever heard of. The unrealistic odds create massive hype … for better or worse. If Hasan was a simple 3-1 favorite, nobody would be foaming at the mouth to scream FRAUD CHECK. The next leg of this upset is Hasan himself. Hopefully, the standout young talent learns some lessons here. Outside of the flashy kicks, he struggled to create meaningful offense with his hands. His step-in elbow was lovely but saw him taken down because he crashed forward too hard. More problematic, Hasan failed to create scrambles and movement from his back. Whether he uses the guard or wrestle-ups, Hasan has much to learn in escaping bottom position. Here’s the rub: that’s okay! Prospects should have more to learn. item.title: Rory McIlroy wins Race to Dubai title for record-equalling eighth time
item.description: Rory McIlroy has won the Race to Dubai title for a record-equalling eighth time, pipping Eugenio Chacarra to the crown. Spaniard Chacarra had held a slender 533.93-point lead over Masters champion McIlroy going into the season finale at Jumeirah Golf Estates. McIlroy, though, overturned that deficit after a blemish-free fourth round of 67 saw him finish on 10 under par, on his own in second, to take a fifth successive European tour crown, matching Colin Montgomerie ’s record of eight Order of Merit titles. Ryder Cup team-mate Tyrrell Hatton , meanwhile, stormed to victory in Dubai, ending the day five shots ahead of second-placed McIlroy to round off a fantastic week. "Winning eight Order of Merits (now called Race to Dubai) was never in my list of goals growing up,” McIlroy said. "I remember Monty being a stalwart of the European tour and playing with him at the London Club in 2008, so to pull up alongside him and win eight of these means the world to me. "I'm proud to be European and part of this tour." Visibly choked up, McIlroy revealed that his dad Gerry has been in hospital since undergoing "a huge operation in September" and dedicated his triumph to him. Rory McIlroy won the Race to Dubai title as Tyrrell Hatton triumphed at the DP World Championship (Getty) He also reflected on the drama of the day and insisted he wasn’t aware of how “back and forth” the title fight with Chacarra was until he reached the 16th. "When I walked to the 16th green I saw Eugenio [Chacarra] was projected one, and when I walked off after my birdie I was projected one,” he added. "Eugenio played pretty good, but none of the chasing pack made a move and thankfully everything fell my way. "I pride myself in my consistency. I finished third last week, second this week. I feel like I've done a good job in recent years of not playing my way out of tournaments like I did earlier in my career." It was heartbreak for Chacarra, who needed to win the tournament to make sure he fended off McIlroy, as well as potentially several other big hitters in the chasing pack. Eugenio Chacarra was pipped to the crown (Getty) However, a final round of 69, which featured six birdies but also three bogeys either side of the turn, saw him come up just short at eight under in a tie for third, with other scores in the final groups also going McIlroy’s way. "It was a good fight. I just came out short. That's the beauty of golf,” he said. "Obviously, when you play with the best in the world, and McIlroy's played here 14, 15 times, you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did. "I played good. I fought. I knew it was going to be a long day, and I tried my best. That's all I can ask for myself to do and that's what we did."

item.title: Detroit Lions Release First Aidan Hutchinson Injury Update
item.description: The Detroit Lions have officially released an injury update on star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson following a frightening incident during Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. According to the team’s official public relations account, Hutchinson is QUESTIONABLE to return with a knee injury. The announcement came after the Lions star went down grabbing his right leg following a first-quarter sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. The injury occurred on New England’s opening offensive possession, turning what should have been an exciting moment for Detroit into an extremely concerning scene. Hutchinson jumped while celebrating the sack before falling to the ground in obvious discomfort. Medical personnel attended to him before he eventually walked off the field under his own power. Although Hutchinson was noticeably limping, he did not require assistance leaving the field. He was subsequently evaluated in the medical tent before making his way to the locker room. Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (97) waves at fans as he walks off the field after 19-9 win over Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Lions Confirm Aidan Hutchinson Knee Injury At 9:54 a.m. ET, the Detroit Lions’ official public relations account released the following update: “#Lions Injury Update: EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, Knee, Questionable” While the questionable designation leaves open the possibility that Hutchinson could return, the Lions have not provided any additional information regarding the severity of his knee injury. The situation is especially concerning given Hutchinson’s history. The former Michigan standout suffered a devastating broken leg during the 2024 season, an injury that ended his year prematurely. Since returning, Hutchinson has reestablished himself as one of the NFL’s premier pass rushers, even setting a franchise sack-streak record earlier this season. His importance to Detroit’s defense cannot be overstated, particularly with the Lions already dealing with multiple significant injuries. The team entered Sunday’s matchup without several defensive contributors, including cornerback D.J. Reed and safety Kerby Joseph, who were ruled out before traveling to Germany . For now, the official update confirms that Hutchinson is dealing with a knee injury, but there has been no confirmed diagnosis or announcement that he will miss additional games. Detroit will undoubtedly be hoping for the best as the Lions await further information on one of their most important defensive players.
